src: U.S. Census Bureau, cartographic boundary file cb_2020_us_cd116_500k
cd.vint: The Census Bureau's lines of the 116th Congress's districts (its file says session 116). The Bureau published no file of the 117th Congress's districts, the Congress the 2020 election chose.
rec: Clerk of the House, Statistics of the 2020 Congressional Election: Vermont elects its U.S. Representative 'AT LARGE'
A single statewide district; Census cb_2020 cd116 file: 1 district, code 00.

src: U.S. Census Bureau, cartographic boundary file cb_2020_us_sldu_500k
sldu.vint: The Census Bureau's 2020 file of legislative districts, the lines it records for the 2018 legislative session year. The Bureau published no file of the lines in use for 2020. Where a state's lines changed in between, the check below or the plan cited stops the map.
rec: 2012 Act 93 (H.789): 13 senatorial districts (Addison, Bennington, Caledonia, Chittenden, Essex-Orleans, Franklin, Grand Isle, Lamoille, Orange, Rutland, Washington, Windham, Windsor)

Vermont General Assembly, 2012 Act 93 (H.789), 'An act relating to reapportioning the final representative districts of the House of Representatives and the senatorial districts of the Senate'; approved May 1, 2012; applies to the 2012 election cycle and thereafter

Used in the 2012 through 2020 elections. Census cb_2020 sldu file: LSY 2018, 13 districts with the same names ('Grand-Isle-Chittenden', 'Chittenden', 'Essex-Orleans'...). The file's ids and names differ from the 2022 file's (e.g. 2020 CGI/CHI/E-O, 2022 GRI/CHC/CHN/CHS/ESX/ORL): match by the act's district names, not ids.
